\begin{exercise} \end{exercise} 1. ch5:5-23

Let $(M,g)$ be a connected Riemannian manifold and $p \in M$. An admissible loop based at $p$ is an admissible curve $\gamma : [a,b] \to M$ such that $\gamma (a) = \gamma (b) = p$. For each such loop $\gamma $, let $P^\gamma $ denote the parallel transport operator $P^\gamma _{ab}: T_pM \to T_pM$ along $\gamma $, and let $\operatorname {Hol}(p) \subseteq \operatorname {GL}(T_pM)$ denote the set of all automorphisms of $T_pM$ obtained in this way: \[ \operatorname {Hol}(p) = \{ P^\gamma : \gamma \text{ is an admissible loop based at } p\} . \]

  1. Show that $\operatorname {Hol}(p)$ is a subgroup of $O(T_pM)$ (the set of all linear isometries of $T_pM$), called the holonomy group at $p$.

  2. Let $\operatorname {Hol}^0(p) \subseteq \operatorname {Hol}(p)$ denote the subset obtained by restricting to loops $\gamma $ that are path-homotopic to the constant loop. Show that $\operatorname {Hol}^0(p)$ is a normal subgroup of $\operatorname {Hol}(p)$, called the restricted holonomy group at $p$.

  3. Given $p,q \in M$, show that there is an isomorphism of $\operatorname {GL}(T_pM)$ with $\operatorname {GL}(T_qM)$ that takes $\operatorname {Hol}(p)$ to $\operatorname {Hol}(q)$.

  4. Show that $M$ is orientable if and only if $\operatorname {Hol}(p) \subseteq \operatorname {SO}(T_pM)$ (the set of linear isometries with determinant $+1$) for some $p \in M$.

  5. Show that $g$ is flat if and only if $\operatorname {Hol}^0(p)$ is the trivial group for some $p \in M$.

\end{exercise}
